Messages.Author: Bob Ellison
Messages.Body:
> 1.  IS this the jyhad newsgroup....????
> 2.  If not what is it??

No. :-)  Try rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad, for Jyhad-specific 
questions and discussion.

> 3.  Can you mail me a Jyhad rarity list?? -- I have no FTP access

Check r.g.t-c.j.  I think there's a list posted relatively frequently.

> My predator is bleeding me wiht his Toreador.
> I block with my Gangrel.

> Since he is the acting Methuselah, I ask him to choose range & strike
> first.

> He is fine with short range, so am I.
> He says "For my strike, Ill punch ya", thus choosing hand damage for his
> strike.
> I play Wolf Claws and punch back.

> Here is where the dispute begins.
> He maintains that he can now play a strike: Dodge card.
> I say because he already chose a strike, he is stuck with it, unless he
> uses a Blur or something.

Once the strike is declared, he has to stick with it.  If he uses Blur,
he'll get additional strikes (if he isn't in torpor first :-).  But
he is still bound by his choice for the first strike.

You can actually be even sneakier.  Wolf Claws isn't a strike card; it is
a strike modifier.  You can declare a strike with hands normally, and
then play the Wolf Claws when you're resolving the strike.  This is
a standard tactic if you are the attacker and are declaring your strike
first.

Moral of the story - Gangrel are best kept at long range. ;-)
